lines.text: One altitude, one speed, one period. A circular orbit has no choice about it.
Thin air. The drag force points backwards along the track.
Backwards. So obviously it slows down.
It does not. It ends up a hundred kilometres lower — and 57 metres a second faster.
The accounting is exact, and it is the reason.
Drag takes energy out of the orbit. Call it one unit.
The orbit drops, and the height it gives up is worth two units.
One went to drag. The other had nowhere to go but into speed.
And it does not settle there.
Lower means denser air, which means more drag, which means lower still.
What you notice first is not the altitude.
A geomagnetic storm heats the thermosphere.
